title: Proof-Carrying Code (Necula)
description: Necula's proof-carrying code ships programs with machine-checkable safety proofs: the host verifies the proof instead of trusting the code. Trust becomes verification, not faith.

demo.code:
import random, hashlib
random.seed(1001)
n=1000
# Proof-carrying sum: compute sum, ship certificate chain; verifier replays.
data=[random.randint(1,100) for _ in range(n)]
total=sum(data)
chain=[]
h="GENESIS"
for x in data:
    h=hashlib.sha256((h+str(x)).encode()).hexdigest()
    chain.append(h)
# verifier: replay
h2="GENESIS"; ok=True
for x,ch in zip(data,chain):
    h2=hashlib.sha256((h2+str(x)).encode()).hexdigest()
    if h2!=ch: ok=False; break
print(f"n=1000 sum={total} chain_len={len(chain)}")
print(f"certificate_head={chain[0][:12]}... tail={chain[-1][:12]}...")
print(f"verifier_replay={'PASS' if ok and h2==chain[-1] else 'FAIL'}")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.output:
n=1000 sum=51102 chain_len=1000
certificate_head=84bd5a56ba24... tail=a45032f0ef16...
verifier_replay=PASS
DEMO_OK
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Code producers attach safety proofs; hosts run the proof checker before execution. Failed proofs mean no execution — the policy is enforced by mathematics.
